newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, soyoil hits contract low.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, soyoil hits contract low.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended mixed on Monday with old crop up on strong cash basis levels and ideas last week's losses would attract renewed buying interest, pit sources said.
Soyoil ended down and a contract low was notched in the July on fund selling tied to bearish technicals.

Soymeal traded lower most of the session but old crop months turned higher late as the May contract surged. Pit sources pointed to short covering ahead of Tuesday's expiry and continued strong cash basis levels. Cash soymeal basis levels on Monday were quoted at $18.00 per ton over July futures, unchanged from Friday.

Most trade sources said they expected Tuesday's expiry to be quiet after open interest in the May soymeal dropped to 2,641 lots as of Friday, down 762 from the previous session. There have been no deliveries posted against the May and none were expected.
The July soyoil contract notched a contract low at 23.60 cent a lb, below the previous low of 23.66 set on November 12.
Soymeal ended $3.50 per ton higher to $2.60 lower with July up $3.00 at $291.80. Soyoil closed 0.19 to 0.07 cent per lb lower with July off 0.17 at 23.80.
Soymeal and soyoil had struggled much of the session with bearish technical and fundamental input.
Technical traders said the charts had been giving off bearish signals since last Monday's sharp break.

Fundamental traders noted indications South America was siphoning business away from the United States despite last week's firmer basis levels. They pointed to lackluster weekly soybean crush and export figures.

USDA on Monday said 5.5 million bushels of soybeans were inspected for export, below trade expectations for eight million to 12 million bushels. Last Thursday's crush figure was also below expectations.

Meanwhile, South Korea bought Brazilian soybeans overnight and was tendering for another cargo. Taiwan was also in for South American soybeans and Thailand was said to be looking for South American supplies for June/July shipment.
New crop months were hit by forecasts for warmer weather and weekend showers. That combination was seen beneficial for soybean germination and early development.
The market continued to react to expectations for a record soybean crop after USDA predicted new crop production could reach 2.6 billion bushels. Some private forecasts have put the crop even higher.

On the day, commercials were buyers of soyoil on the break. ADM and Cargill Inc each bought 400 lots July soyoil, Produce Grain bought 100 July and Term Commodities bought 150 December, pit sources said.
Prudential Securities, Dean Witter and Tenco Inc each sold 300 lots July.
In soymeal, R.J. O'Brien and Prudential each bought 300 July and Dean Witter bought 300 December.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 22,972 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 14,000 lots, against Friday's 14,406.
